subtitle: The Hill That Would Not Bow

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a craggy Aravalli ridge, half in sun, half in shadow
panels.action: Maharana Amar Singh I stands on a rocky height in war-worn armor, one hand resting on his sheathed sword as the distant outline of the Mughal camp smokes on the horizon under a pale dawn sky

dialogue.text: In 1615, after forty years of hill war, Maharana Amar Singh I of Mewar faced a question no blade could answer: how do you keep a kingdom’s honor when its strength is almost gone?

i18n.hi: १६१५ में, चालीस बरस की पहाड़ी जंग के बाद, मेवाड़ के महाराणा अमर सिंह प्रथम के सामने सवाल था – ताकत ढल रही हो तो इज़्ज़त कैसे बची रहे?

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view over the Aravalli hills, panning from ruined fields to a distant Mughal column
panels.action: Terraced fields lie parched and broken between rugged hills, thin villagers and scattered Rajput horsemen watching as a disciplined line of Mughal troops winds like an iron serpent through the valley below

dialogue.text: For two generations, from Maharana Pratap to his son Amar Singh, Mewar bled in the Aravalli hills, trading stone forts and scorched fields against the vast armies of the Mughal empire.

i18n.hi: दो पीढ़ियों से, महाराणा प्रताप से लेकर बेटे अमर सिंह तक, अरावली की घाटियों में मेवाड़ ने पत्थर के किले और जली धरती से मुग़ल साम्राज्य की फौजों को रोके रखा।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Amar Singh in armor beside a weathered banner of Mewar
panels.action: Maharana Amar Singh I, face lined beyond his years, stands in a rocky redoubt above a narrow pass, the sun catching his mail and the frayed saffron standard of Mewar that droops behind him in a faint wind

dialogue.text: Amar Singh had grown to manhood in this war, inheriting his father’s oath to keep Mewar free, and also the cost: burned harvests, broken tanks, and a people driven again and again into the hills.

i18n.hi: अमर सिंह इसी जंग में जवान हुए, पिता की कसम विरासत में मिली – मेवाड़ आज़ाद रहेगा – और साथ ही उसकी कीमत भी: जली फसलें, सूखे तलाब, और लोग बार‑बार पहाड़ों में शरण लेते।

panels.shot: montage wide of earlier Mughal-Rajput encounters, slightly desaturated to imply past
panels.action: A visual montage shows a timeline: the ghostly silhouette of Akbar before besieged Chittor, Maharana Pratap riding hard at Haldighati, and later, Mughal standards planted near ruined hill forts while smoke rises from the valleys

dialogue.text: Akbar had broken Chittor in 1568, yet Mewar’s heartland slipped from his grasp. Haldighati did not end the struggle. By Jahangir’s reign, hill warfare had become a grinding habit neither side could finish.

i18n.hi: अकबर ने १५६८ में चित्तौड़ तोड़ डाला, पर मेवाड़ का दिल उसके हाथ से फिसलता रहा। हल्दीघाटी से लड़ाई थमी नहीं। जहाँगीर के वक्त तक पहाड़ी जंग ऐसी पिसाई बन गई जिसे कोई पक्ष ख़त्म न कर सका।

panels.shot: wide of the Mughal imperial camp near the Aravalli foothills
panels.action: A vast Mughal camp spreads across a plain: pavilions striped in red and white, elephants chained by pickets, smiths hammering, scribes bent over scrolls as couriers gallop in from the direction of the hills

dialogue.text: In 1613, Jahangir turned to his son Prince Khurram, the future Shah Jahan, to bring Mewar to terms. The prince drove his campaigns close along the Aravallis, burning villages, seizing passes, tightening the ring.

i18n.hi: १६१३ में जहाँगीर ने बेटे शहज़ादा खुर्रम – भावी शाहजहाँ – को मेवाड़ झुकाने का काम सौंपा। खुर्रम ने अरावली की नस‑नस पर चढ़ाई की, गाँव जलाए, दर्रे कब्ज़े में लिए, घेरे को कस दिया।

panels.shot: interior medium shot in a dim Mewar council hall
panels.action: By lamplight inside a stone hall, Amar Singh sits at a low desk strewn with letters and accounts, his armor laid aside, as outside the open arch a thin line of displaced villagers winds past the fort gate

dialogue.text: The chronicles speak of Amar Singh’s stubborn raids and sudden marches. Yet by 1615, reports of emptied granaries, scattered clansmen and Mughal-controlled plains forced a different kind of council.

i18n.hi: इतिहास अमर सिंह की ज़िद्दी धावों और अचानक कूचों का ज़िक्र करता है। मगर १६१५ तक खाली कोठार, बिखरे बिरादर और मुग़ल के क़ब्ज़े वाले मैदानी इलाक़े नई तरह की सलाह माँग रहे थे।

panels.shot: close-up on Amar Singh’s face, lit by a single lamp
panels.action: A tight close-up shows Amar Singh’s eyes in the lamplight, tired yet steady, his jaw clenched as he listens to unseen voices debating around him while a faint map of Mewar lies rolled out before him

dialogue.text: Later memory in Mewar remembers hot words in that hall. Some urged one last stand. Others pointed to starving villages and said, as traditions record, that a ruler’s dharma is also to spare his land.

i18n.hi: मेवाड़ की यादों में उस दरबार की गरम बातें बस गई हैं। कुछ आख़िरी भिड़ंत पर उतारू थे। कुछ भूखे गाँवों की ओर इशारा कर बोले – जैसा रिवाज़ों में दर्ज है – राजधर्म ये भी है कि धरती को भी बचाया जाए।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Amar Singh rising, hand on sword hilt
panels.action: Amar Singh rises from his seat, hand resting on the hilt of his sheathed sword, his gaze turned toward the dark window where distant fires glimmer in the plains below

dialogue.speaker: maharana_amar_singh_i
dialogue.text: If the steel of these hills cannot break them, perhaps our terms can.

i18n.hi: अगर इन पहाड़ियों की तलवार इन्हें न तोड़ पाई, तो शायद हमारी शर्तें तोड़ें।

panels.shot: wide shot of emissaries riding from a hill fort toward the Mughal camp
panels.action: A small group of Rajput horsemen, unarmored and carrying white cloths tied to their lances, pick their way down a stony path toward the distant sprawl of the Mughal encampment on the plain

dialogue.text: Envoys rode from fort to camp. Mewar did not walk in with folded hands. Through messages carried over these harsh tracks began a slow crafting of peace, word by tested word.

i18n.hi: दूत किले से छावनी दौड़े। मेवाड़ झुकी गर्दन लेकर नहीं गया। इन ऊबड़‑खाबड़ रास्तों से जो पैग़ाम चले, उनमें शब्द‑शब्द तौलकर धीरे‑धीरे सुलह गढ़ी गई।

panels.shot: interior Mughal audience tent, medium wide showing Prince Khurram
panels.action: Inside a richly furnished Mughal tent, Prince Khurram sits on a low throne-like seat, composed and young, listening as a Rajput emissary bows slightly, while Persian scribes sit nearby with reed pens poised

dialogue.text: Mu'tamad Khan’s Iqbalnama remembers Prince Khurram at the center of these talks. In his pavilion, Rajput emissaries laid out what Mewar could and could not yield.

i18n.hi: मुतमद ख़ाँ के ‘इक़बालनामा’ में इन बातों के बीच शहज़ादा खुर्रम का ज़िक्र है। उसके शामियाने में राजपूत वफ्द ने साफ़ रख दिया कि मेवाड़ क्या दे सकता है और क्या नहीं।

panels.shot: split composition showing Amar Singh in a stone hall and Jahangir in a marble pavilion
panels.action: On one side, Amar Singh sits in a plain stone chamber with his advisors; on the other, Jahangir reclines in a carved marble pavilion in distant Ajmer, both figures listening as messengers speak before them

dialogue.text: At Ajmer, Jahangir weighed reports from his son and his scribes. In the hills, Amar Singh weighed his ancestors’ oaths. Between them, a settlement slowly took shape.

i18n.hi: अजमेर में जहाँगीर ने बेटे और अपने मुंशी की रिपोर्टें तौलीं। पहाड़ियों में अमर सिंह ने अपने बाप‑दादों की सौगंधें तौलीं। दोनों के बीच एक समझौते की शक्ल उभरने लगी।

panels.shot: medium detail shot of a manuscript page in Persian script, with a royal seal
panels.action: A close view shows a thick manuscript page covered in neat Persian script, a large Mughal seal impressed in red at the bottom, as a hand places a smaller Rajput signet ring beside it on the low desk

dialogue.text: The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri records the agreed terms. Mewar would accept Mughal suzerainty, send its heir to court, and serve in imperial campaigns as other Rajput houses did.

i18n.hi: ‘तुज़ुक‑ए‑जहाँगीरी’ में तय शर्तें लिखी हैं। मेवाड़ मुग़ल बादशाही सरपरस्ती मानेगा, अपना वारिस दरबार भेजेगा, और बाकी राजपूत घरानों की तरह बादशाही मुहिमों में शरीक होगा।

panels.shot: medium wide showing an unused bridal palanquin covered and still
panels.action: A covered, ornate bridal palanquin stands unused in a courtyard, half in shadow, pigeons perched on its carved frame while beyond it the walls of a Rajput palace rise

dialogue.text: Yet two points set Mewar apart. Unlike many Rajput states, no daughter of Amar Singh’s house would be given in marriage to the Mughal emperor’s family. On this, Mewar held firm.

i18n.hi: पर दो बातें मेवाड़ को अलग करती रहीं। बहुत से राजपूत राज्यों के उलट, अमर सिंह के घर की कोई बेटी मुग़ल ख़ानदान को न दी जाएगी। इस पर मेवाड़ अड़ा रहा।

panels.shot: distant wide of ruined Chittor under a blazing noon sun
panels.action: The shattered walls and empty towers of Chittor fort rise stark against a bleached sky, grass growing between stones, with no sign of repair or scaffolding anywhere on the long scarred ramparts

dialogue.text: Chittor, taken by Akbar decades earlier, would be held by the Mughals. The treaty, as Jahangir notes, forbade its rebuilding or refortification. The great citadel would remain a ruin, a silent memory.

i18n.hi: दशकों पहले अकबर के हाथ गई चित्तौड़ मुग़लों के पास ही रहेगी। जहाँगीर के लिखे मुताबिक़, समझौता उसके दोबारा बसाने या दुर्ग बनाने पर रोक लगाता था। वह महाकिला खंडहर ही रहेगा, ख़ामोश याद की तरह।

panels.shot: medium shot of a young Rajput prince (Karan Singh) preparing to depart
panels.action: A young Rajput prince, bearing the features of Amar Singh, tightens the cinch of his horse as attendants adjust his cloak; behind him, older nobles watch with mixed pride and unease

dialogue.text: Instead of a bride, Mewar would send a son. Prince Karan Singh, Amar Singh’s heir, was chosen to stand at the Mughal court as Mewar’s face and pledge.

i18n.hi: दुल्हन की जगह मेवाड़ बेटा देगा। राजकुमार करण सिंह – अमर सिंह का उत्तराधिकारी – को चुना गया कि वह मुग़ल दरबार में मेवाड़ का चेहरा और गिरवी बनकर खड़ा हो।

panels.shot: wide shot of Karan Singh’s small retinue approaching a grand Mughal city gate
panels.action: Karan Singh’s mounted party approaches an immense Mughal city gate where elephants stand caparisoned and guards in bright uniforms watch; beyond the archway, domes and minarets shimmer in the distance

dialogue.text: The Tuzuk describes Karan Singh’s reception. At the imperial court, he received robes of honor and rank. Mewar’s prince bowed, but behind him stood a kingdom that had not been fully broken.

i18n.hi: तुज़ुक में करण सिंह की बर्ज़ीदारी का ज़िक्र है। बादशाही दरबार में उसे ख़िलअतें और ओहदा मिला। मेवाड़ का राजकुमार झुका, मगर उसके पीछे एक ऐसा राज्य खड़ा था जो पूरी तरह टूटा नहीं था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Amar Singh on the ramparts, watching a distant dust trail
panels.action: Back in the hills, Amar Singh stands upon a fort wall as a faint plume of dust in the far distance marks the path his son has taken toward the Mughal domains

dialogue.speaker: maharana_amar_singh_i
dialogue.text: May he carry our name without letting it be swallowed.

i18n.hi: वह हमारा नाम लेकर जाए, पर उसे किसी के पेट में न गलने दे।

panels.shot: interior medium of Amar Singh in a quieter, less martial setting
panels.action: Amar Singh sits in a shaded courtyard, now in simpler garments, overseeing scribes and officers discussing revenue and irrigation rather than war, as children play quietly near a stone tank

dialogue.text: Rajasthani traditions later say Amar Singh withdrew from public life in sorrow after the treaty, troubled by the oath he had bent. The records do show that open war with the empire ceased in his time.

i18n.hi: राजस्थानी परंपराएँ कहती हैं कि संधि के बाद अमर सिंह ने दुख में राजकाज से हाथ खींच लिया, कसम ढीली करने का बोझ उन्हें सालता रहा। रिकॉर्ड इतना ज़रूर कहते हैं कि उनके ज़माने में बादशाह से खुली जंग थम गई।

panels.shot: wide of Mewar’s countryside showing signs of slow recovery
panels.action: The camera looks over revived fields in the Mewar plains, oxen ploughing, small shrines rebuilt beside irrigation channels, with distant hills still crowned by old forts now quiet

dialogue.text: With peace, fields that had been battle grounds became farms again. Taxes flowed more steadily; caravans crossed the plains with less fear. Mewar remained under its own Rana, though within an emperor’s shadow.

i18n.hi: सुलह के साथ जंग के मैदानी खेत फिर से खेती बने। लगान ढंग से आने लगा; काफ़िले मैदानों को कम ख़ौफ़ से पार करने लगे। मेवाड़ अपना राणा रखकर भी एक बादशाह की परछाईं में रहा।

panels.shot: close-up of an older Amar Singh looking at a faded banner of Mewar
panels.action: In a dim store-room, an older Amar Singh touches a faded saffron banner hung carefully on a wall, his face unreadable as dust motes dance in a shaft of light from a high lattice

dialogue.text: Among Rajputs, Amar Singh’s choice has been judged in many ways: some call it a scar, others a shield. What is clear is that he chose to preserve a weakened state rather than gamble it on one last blaze.

i18n.hi: राजपूतों में अमर सिंह के फ़ैसले पर कई तरह के फ़ैसले दिए गए – कोई इसे दाग़ कहता है, कोई ढाल। इतना साफ़ है कि उन्होंने कमजोर हो चुके राज्य को बचाना चुना, न कि आख़िरी आग में दाँव पर लगाना।

panels.shot: final wide shot over the Aravalli range at sunset, with ruined Chittor in silhouette
panels.action: The sun sets behind the jagged line of the Aravallis, Chittor’s broken outline dark against the orange sky, while in the nearer valleys small, living fires of villages begin to glow

dialogue.text: The peace of 1615 did not make Amar Singh a conqueror, nor a traitor; it made him the man who chose that Mewar’s story should continue, even if its proudest fort remained a ruin on the horizon.

i18n.hi: १६१५ की सुलह ने अमर सिंह को न फ़तह का नायक बनाया, न ही गद्दार; उसने उन्हें वह आदमी बनाया जिसने ठाना कि मेवाड़ की कहानी चलती रहे – चाहे उसका सबसे गर्वीला किला दूर क्षितिज पर खंडहर ही क्यों न बना रहे।

title_i18n.en: Amar Singh I Makes Peace with Jahangir
title_i18n.hi: अमर सिंह प्रथम – जहाँगीर से सुलह

subtitle_i18n.en: The Hill That Would Not Bow
subtitle_i18n.hi: जो पहाड़ी झुकने को तैयार न थी
